repo_notes.content: Docker sidecar (POSIX sh, Alpine) that discovers PostgreSQL databases at runtime, regenerates PgDog's pgdog.toml/users.toml, and reloads PgDog via SIGHUP on change. No compiled code, no framework — shell + Docker only.

Loop: entrypoint.sh polls generate-config.sh every POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 300). generate-config.sh lists non-template DBs via psql -t -A, writes .tmp files, cmp -s-compares, atomically mv's into place only when changed, then pkill -HUP pgdog.
SIGHUP works because sidecar and PgDog share a PID namespace (pid: 'service:pgdog') and run as the same UID (default 1000) — mismatched UID makes pkill -HUP silently fail.
Passthrough auth (enabled_plain): passwords in users.toml must match PostgreSQL backend passwords exactly; the sidecar does not manage PG users. Never log passwords.
versions.env pins the PgDog image (single source of truth); production pins versions, test compose deliberately uses :main to catch upstream breakage early.

Critical test rule: never verify the dynamic function by manually invoking generate-config.sh — the autonomous polling loop is the feature; tests wait for it to detect changes (33-assertion integration suite on ports 5433/6433).
See AGENTS.md for pitfalls (PG18+ volume mounts, psql -t whitespace, flock, set -e in loops).
